history.dynasty: Pallava (King Narasimha Varma, 9th century per wall inscriptions)
history.summary: The famous Narasimha shrine of the Nellore region, on the summit of Narasimhakonda hill about 15 km west of Nellore on the southern bank of the Penna (Pinakini), under Devarapalem panchayat. The Brahma Purana legend says the Saptarishis performed a yagna here with seven yagna kundams (now seven koneru tanks), and sage Kasyapa installed Lakshmi Narasimha on the hill. Wall inscriptions attribute the cave-shaped sanctum and six-tier gopuram to the Pallava king Narasimha Varma in the 9th century; the main deity is a 10-ft black-stone Narasimha slaying Hiranyakashipu. FLAG: CSV name 'Sri Narasimhaswamy Temple' is generic; identity as the Vedagiri/Narasimhakonda shrine is provisional (town corrected from Nellore to Narasimhakonda); coordinates are the Narasimhakonda locality, not a temple POI match.

name: Sri Narasimhaswamy Temple
town_description: Narasimhakonda is a hill village (Devarapalem panchayat) about 15 km west of Nellore, known almost entirely for the ancient Vedagiri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple on its summit. Set in the lush Vedagiri hills on the Penna river, it draws pilgrims year-round and is crowded during Narasimha Jayanti.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport, about 120-140 km away.
travel.railway: Nellore railway station, about 15-20 km east.
travel.road: About 15 km west of Nellore by road; buses and taxis run from Nellore to the hill; a climb or vehicle access reaches the summit temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Narasimha Jayanti (April-May) and the May Brahmotsavams are the peak festival period.
